What if every citizen in a nation was required to be an actor in a movie? What if citizens got drafted into movies?

Why not? I mean some nations require their young male adults to serve a mandatory two years in the military; if we could draft people to go train and sometimes die in meaningless wars, then what's stopping my idea?

I think it would be beneficial if people were drafted into movie experiences. Its an intimate experience with the performing arts, providing young participants with the chance to pretend to be someone their not. I could see acting experience to be a great skill for employment in other areas; we often want our employees to act a certain way, put up a cheery facade and accompany any customer's needs. Acting could only be a boon to employees to help them put up the masks required to participate in the day-to-day jobs and satisfy customers.

But my main reason for this is documentation. We humans are often very morbid in our thinking, wondering how exactly it is that we are to leave behind a legacy will live on when we die. People have been dying a long time now undocumented, viz. no pictures, no video recordings, no audio recordings, and not even writing fragments remain to represent the once living person who is no more.

My idea represents a participatory society where its members engage in the arts that reach the masses, that is, movies. The movies would be documentation of our time in society. We could hear of John Doe and remember that he acted as a minor character in Marvel Movie #79, giving a face to a name. John Doe's marginal legacy would live on!

But how would it be decided who gets drafted into a leading role or not. Or who gets drafted into a good script or a terrible script. What about people being drafted into pornographic films? They're still considered art. Would people wishing to not be captured on film be draft dodgers?
